spec_notes: spec.md is a short verification plan rather than a requirement list; it is silent on most unstated conditions (person per browser, bot and conversation naming, Since you were away semantics, storage failure, damaged data). It marks three decisions as "Default:" (one saved operator token serves all personas; identity, type and readers are app-managed and only business fields of the same type may change; a stopped server leaves tasks Interrupted for explicit retry). It decides without marking: tokens kept out of client storage, confirm-twice and stale proposals produce one change or a conflict, cancellation keeps finished steps, and responses project only the selected persona. It pins choices a correct product need not share: Chrome UI-1 checking light and dark rendering at 1440 and 390 px, and an "original, editorial" design. No contradiction with the request found.
tests_notes: Most HTTP tests cover several behaviours at once (TC-6: count, unreadable record, clarify, proposal, reject, confirm twice, conflict, readers refusal and restart; TC-3: pending, failure, retry and duplicate requestId). Tests are tied to internals: they call createServer({directory, token}) and the private action protocol (/api/action with action names, requestId, proposal and steer fields), TC-14 parses index.html for data-limit attributes, TC-16 renames the data folder and expects "ENOENT" and the task id in console.error, TC-18 and TC-19 pin exact result wording, TC-7 pins ORD-1005 and the readers array, TC-22 pins the title/detail derivation, TC-11/12/20 test client-side helpers in public/rules.js. Timing dependence: STANDIN_STEP_MS 35/80/300 with fixed delays (TC-8 65 ms, TC-16 700 ms). All of these would fail on another correct build. test/browser.cjs is reported as passing by npm test but does not run there (guarded by NODE_TEST_CONTEXT), so the accessible names, focus and narrow-width behaviour have no automated check in the suite.
maintainer: All state lives in one workspace.json snapshot that is deep-cloned and rewritten for every action and every task step, with in-memory state advancing only after the write; any change to the store or to error handling around it (as the stuck pending reply shows) needs care because respond(), the task worker and actions each recover differently. lib/workspace.js mixes routing, validation and rules in one switch keyed by action strings that the page and tests also hard-code, and public/app.js relies on revision counters, string-keyed re-render caching and data-focus keys to keep focus and polling consistent, which is easy to break silently.
